haiku-low.q1: Consecutive breaches reach 3 and no incident is open for that service and rule. A breach needs error rate above 2% and at least 500 requests.
haiku-low.q2: Each breach is added to the open incident only. Nobody is paged, and the breach is recorded on the incident.
haiku-low.q3: Ten clear minutes in a row (error rate below 1%) resolve it. A resolved notice goes to everyone in page_log. A later breach opens a new incident, needing 3 breaches in a row.
haiku-low.q4: Primary is paged first, then secondary, then EM. Each step follows a 5-minute timer, and escalation stops on ack or resolution. The EM is the last level, with no timer after it.
haiku-low.q5: If the push call fails, the same person gets an SMS. The page_log row is still written and the escalation timer is still set. If both fail, page_log records both failures and escalation continues.
haiku-low.q6: Everyone with a page_log row for the incident gets a resolved notice, push with SMS fallback. Pending escalation stops because the timer check finds the incident resolved and does nothing.
haiku-low.q7: In rule_state in Postgres, one row per service and rule. A non-breach resets consecutive breaches to 0. A breach or a rate at or above 1% resets clear minutes to 0.
haiku-low.q8: Each evaluator claims the minute in rule_state, which only succeeds if the last claimed minute is older. The other stops. A unique index on open incidents blocks a second incident.
haiku-low.q9: A 5-minute timer triggers each step. It reads the incident and page_log, does nothing if acked, resolved, or the level is already paged, and otherwise pages the next level.
haiku-low.q10: The paging provider calls the webhook with the page id. The manager sets acked_at and acked_by if empty. When the scheduled timer fires, it sees the ack and does nothing.
haiku-low.q11: At the moment of paging, the manager asks the schedule service who holds that level now, so the 09:00 handover is respected.
haiku-low.q12: It reads the page_log rows for that incident, which record everyone who was paged, and sends the notice to each of them.

sonnet.q1: 3 consecutive breaching evaluations (error rate above 2% with at least 500 requests in the 5-minute window) AND no incident already open for that service and rule. A unique index on open incidents also blocks a second one.
sonnet.q2: The breach is added to the existing incident and nobody is paged. Breaches are recorded on the incident only.
sonnet.q3: An open incident resolves after 10 clear minutes in a row (error rate under 1%). A minute at or above 1% resets the clear count. A later breach opens a new incident, which needs 3 breaches in a row again.
sonnet.q4: Primary immediately when the incident opens (level 1). If not acked or resolved, secondary (level 2) when the 5-minute timer fires, then EM (level 3) 5 minutes after that. No timer is set after the EM.
sonnet.q5: If push fails, an SMS is sent to the same person. The page_log row is still written and the 5-minute escalation timer is still set. If push and SMS both fail, page_log records both failures and the timer still runs, so escalation moves on.
sonnet.q6: Everyone with a page_log row for the incident gets a resolved notice, by push with SMS fallback. Pending escalation stops: when the timer fires, step 6 finds the incident resolved and does nothing.
sonnet.q7: In Postgres, in the rule_state table (one row per service and rule). A breach adds 1 to consecutive breaches and sets clear minutes to 0. A non-breach (including a window under 500 requests) sets consecutive breaches to 0. Under 1% adds 1 to clear minutes, otherwise clear minutes resets to 0.
sonnet.q8: Each evaluator first claims the minute by updating rule_state only if its last claimed minute is older than this one. The first to claim applies the result and the other stops. A unique index on open incidents also blocks a second open incident for the same service and rule.
sonnet.q9: A 5-minute timer on the timer queue triggers each step. The incident manager reads the incident and page_log. It does nothing if the incident is acked or resolved, or if the next level is already in page_log. Otherwise it asks the schedule service for the next level and pages them.
sonnet.q10: The paging provider calls our webhook with its page id. The incident manager finds the page_log row and sets acked_at and acked_by on the incident if they are empty, so the first ack wins. The scheduled timer is not cancelled. When it fires, step 6 sees the ack and does nothing.
sonnet.q11: At page time. The incident manager asks the schedule service who is primary, or the next level, at that moment, for each page, so a 09:00 handover is respected.
sonnet.q12: It reads the page_log rows for that incident in Postgres and sends the notice to everyone with a row.
